idiom_name: struct or final class (actor for conversational state) with constructor-injected services, graph built at the app entry point
implementation_notes: The standard library has no DI container, so the facade is a hand-written struct or final class whose initializer takes the fine-grained services, with the graph assembled once in the app entry point or an AppEnvironment struct - constructor injection is the idiom, and that component is the coarse boundary. Actors are the language-level tool for the stateful variant: an actor-isolated facade serialises access to conversation state and makes call sites await, which replaces hand-managed locks, while async facade methods let the workflow await each service without blocking a thread. Keep the plain struct or class when the facade is stateless and its callers are UI-bound; choose the actor when it owns mutable per-conversation state, and keep the boundary coarse in both cases so the call sites do not orchestrate the services themselves.
pitfalls: Protocol existentials (any PricingService) are easy to inject but erase associated types and add indirection; use generics or primary associated types when the service has requirements.
An actor facade's methods are async and re-entrant between awaits, so two workflows can interleave; re-check the conversation state after every suspension point instead of assuming exclusivity.
Closures stored by a service that capture the facade create retain cycles (and leak the dependency graph); capture [weak self] or keep the dependency non-escaping.
